“A third party angrier than the victim becomes an aggressor” is a test of who owns the anger

Akira Kawashima of Kirin once said on『川島・山内のマンガ沼』,「被害者より怒っている第三者は加害者だ」—roughly, a third party angrier than the victim becomes an aggressor. This is not a scientific law and it should not be used to silence third-party anger. Research on third-party punishment and solidarity shows that outsiders can help enforce norms and support victims. At the same time, online outrage can be reinforced by social feedback and can acquire rewards unrelated to the victim's recovery. This essay reads Kawashima's line as a self-check: when did the subject of my anger move from the victim to me?
